title: Setting up Drizzle ORM
idea: Drizzle is an ORM, a library that turns JavaScript calls into SQL. `src/db/index.js` creates one `db` from `DATABASE_URL`; every other file imports it.
points: `drizzle-orm` builds the queries; the `pg` driver opens connections and sends the SQL.
`drizzle(process.env.DATABASE_URL)` returns `db`, backed by a pool of reusable `pg` connections.
`drizzle-kit` is a dev-only command-line tool; `drizzle.config.js` points it at the schema and database.
`import 'dotenv/config'` loads `.env` into `process.env` before the client reads it.

parts.label: Scheme
parts.note: Says this is a PostgreSQL connection.

parts.label: Password
parts.note: Set by `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. A demo value; use a strong one anywhere real.

parts.label: Host
parts.note: Your own machine. The published port forwards traffic to the container.

code.title: Install
code.caption: Run these in the project root. `-D` saves `drizzle-kit` as a development dependency.

code.title: The db client
code.caption: In the project, put `import 'dotenv/config'` first so `.env` loads. Here the book supplies `DATABASE_URL`.

walk.text: One `db` for the whole app. A string argument is a connection string.
`execute` runs raw SQL. Rows come back in `result.rows`.
End the pool, or the process never exits.

code.title: drizzle.config.js
code.caption: Settings for `drizzle-kit`, in the project root. It cannot run here.

walk.text: `drizzle-kit` runs outside your app, so it loads `.env` itself.
The database dialect, and the file that defines your tables.
The folder for migration files, saved SQL that changes tables. `generate` writes them there.
The connection string, read from the environment.

pitfalls: If `DATABASE_URL` is unset, `drizzle()` still returns `db`; the first query fails with 'Failed query'.
`dotenv` never overrides variables already set in your shell, so an old value wins.
Keep `.env` out of git. Add it to `.gitignore`.

quiz.code:
const result = await db.execute(sql`select 1 as ok`);
console.log(result.rows);
quiz.why: `result.rows` is an array with one object per row. The column alias `ok` becomes the key.

takeaway: One `db` from `DATABASE_URL`, created once and imported everywhere.
